questions.prompt: In a star topology, what is the single point of failure?
options: The device at the edge with the most traffic

questions.prompt: In a star, a damaged cable to one computer takes the whole network down.
Most office and home networks today are wired in which topology? (one word)
What's the main strength of a mesh topology?
options: Reliable data transmission: if one link fails, traffic takes another path
It needs no configuration at all

questions.prompt: And the drawback the reading gives for mesh?
options: Only one device can send at a time
Redundancy results in additional traffic (and more cables and ports to pay for)
The hub is a single point of failure

questions.prompt: A full mesh connects 5 devices. How many links does it need in total? (a number)
In a full mesh of 8 devices, how many links does each device need? (a number)
A university joins one star network per building back to a core switch, in levels. Which topology is that?
Tree topologies are easy and cheap to configure.
